quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If your front wheel locks, what should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
Release the front brake right away and use only the rear brake.
Keep the front wheel locked until you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake immediately and then apply it again.

questions.question: What is one of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to keep your headlight on. Use your high beam both day and night when it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: You see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to move.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you approach an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space and slow down. Always be ready to stop near an emergency scene.

questions.question: If you carry a load on your motorcycle, where should it be placed?

options.text: Over the rear axle.
On the gas tank in front of you.
Piled against the back of the seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over the rear axle.
questions.explanation: Keep loads over or in front of the rear axle. Only experienced riders should carry loads on their motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding over grooved pavement in a work zone, what should you do?

options.text: Look down to watch for road changes.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Move to the edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up when riding through a work zone. Ride slowly over the grooved pavement.

questions.question: There is usually an oily strip in the center of a traffic lane. What should motorcyclists do?

options.text: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
Do not worry about the oil and grease.
Find the lane with the least amount of oil and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
questions.explanation: Avoid riding on oil and grease buildup. The oily strip is usually only about two feet wide, so you can often ride to the left or right side and still stay in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. This sign warns drivers that the road ahead will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: What should you tell your passenger to do before riding?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before you do.
Sit as far back as possible.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
questions.explanation: Ask your passenger to wait and get on after you start the engine. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What should passengers do?

options.text: Look over their shoulder when taking a turn or curve.
Never hold onto the rider.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over their shoulder when taking a turn or curve.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to look over your shoulder in the direction of any turn or curve. This helps you and your motorcycle lean in the right direction.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, which part of the lane should you ride in?

options.text: Right
Center
Left

questions.correctAnswerText: Center
questions.explanation: When being passed, the center of the lane is usually safest for a motorcyclist. Riding near the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding far from it may cause the driver to return to your lane unsafely.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: You can go faster than the speed limit until you finish passing.
You can ignore no passing zone markings if you started in a passing zone.
You must follow the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must follow the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must complete all passes at the posted speed limit. You can only pass in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders be positioned?

options.text: In the front.
Just behind the lead rider.
In the rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them and help if needed.

questions.question: When should you keep a longer distance between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When the road is slippery.
When there is light traffic.
When you can see through the vehicle ahead to check traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road is slippery.
questions.explanation: You need more distance to stop when the road is slippery, when you cannot see around the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy. Use at least a four-second following distance in these situations.

questions.question: When carrying a load on your motorcycle, how should you secure it?

options.text: As low as possible.
As high as possible.
Attached to a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep loads as low as possible. Putting a load on a sissy bar raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and can affect balance.

questions.question: When making a U-turn, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it can tip the bike over.
Use the front brake to keep the motorcycle stable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it can tip the bike over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it can cause the bike to tip over. Use only the rear brake to control your speed.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: On the outside of the curve.
On the inside of the curve.
Wherever you can safely handle road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever you can safely handle road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position based on the road and traffic, and change it as needed.

questions.question: At an intersection with no traffic control, two vehicles arrive at the same time. What should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to tell the other vehicle to go first.
Go through the intersection and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: When arriving at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the part of your lane where other drivers can see you as soon as possible.
Stop at the stop sign or signal, then proceed normally.
Flash your lights and use your horn to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of your lane where other drivers can see you as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, position yourself so other drivers can see you at the earliest possible moment.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: During the day.
At dusk.
At night.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Always wear bright colors and reflective materials, even during daylight hours.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: This regulatory sign tells drivers what traffic laws apply in this area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When carrying a load, where should it be secured?

options.text: As high as possible.
As low as possible.
On a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Secure loads low to keep the motorcycle balanced. A high load can upset the balance.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Slow down as the dog approaches, then quickly speed up and ride away.
Swerve around the dog.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as the dog approaches, then quickly speed up and ride away.
questions.explanation: Slow down and downshift as the dog gets closer. Then quickly accelerate away from the dog.

questions.question: What formation should a group of riders use?

options.text: Always single-file.
It depends on the situation.
Always staggered.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is best for most group riding. Switch to single-file when turning, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When someone is tailgating you.
When you are slowing down quickly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are slowing down quickly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are not as noticeable as car brake lights. Flash your brake light when slowing suddenly so other riders will notice you are stopping.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of the lane should you use?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
Wherever you feel most comfortable.
The right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of the lane to avoid car doors opening, people stepping out, and cars pulling out. Stay alert and adjust your position as needed.
